data.title: Hallador Energy Receives Regulatory Approval for $1B, 12-Year Capacity Sale
data.description:
Hallador Energy Company () (“Hallador” or the “Company”), a vertically integrated independent power producer, today announced that the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission has approved its previously announced 12-year capacity agreement with a subsidiary of a utility. The Commission’s order, issued on November 18, 2026, satisfies the regulatory approval condition to the agreement, which is now effective.

The agreement, entered into on May 1, 2026, and announced on May 6, 2026, is expected to generate more than $1 billion in capacity revenue from the Company’s Merom Generating Station through mid-2040. Priced at more than twice Hallador’s historical capacity pricing, the agreement nearly doubled Hallador’s forward sales book when announced in May. Subsequent agreements have increased the Company’s total forward sales book to approximately $3 billion.

“This contract provides a long-term source of revenue at more than twice Hallador's historical capacity pricing,” said Brent Bilsland, President and Chief Executive Officer of Hallador. “It allows us to retain the ability to sell Merom’s energy separately, and earn additional revenue from the power the plant produces.”

Deliveries begin with a smaller volume of accredited capacity in late 2028, increasing to approximately two-thirds of the Company’s accredited capacity beginning in 2029 and continuing through the end of the term. The capacity price remains fixed throughout the 12-year term.

Capacity payments compensate Hallador for keeping power generation capability available to meet demand. The agreement is capacity-only and does not include the sale of energy.

“We’ve put long-term contracts in place and made significant progress on our plans to grow our power business,” said Bilsland. “This approval demonstrates that Indiana’s Regulators are still supporting the growth of data centers in Indiana.”

About Hallador Energy Company

Hallador Energy Company () is a vertically integrated independent power producer based in Terre Haute, Indiana. The Company has two core businesses: Hallador Power Company, LLC, which produces electricity and provides accredited capacity at its one-gigawatt Merom Generating Station, and Sunrise Coal, LLC, which produces and supplies fuel to Merom and other companies. For more information, visit www.halladorenergy.com.

These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. data.title: CBOT wheat rises on Black Sea export worries
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures rebounded from a multi-month low on Thursday as a lack of diplomatic progress towards de-escalation in Russia's war in Ukraine elevated worries about Black Sea shipments, analysts said.

  • Russian President Vladimir Putin ruled out negotiations for a Black Sea ceasefire after Ukraine destroyed part of a bridge linking Russia to Crimea.

  • The International Grains Council raised its forecast for 2026/27 global wheat production by 6 million metric tons to 826 million tons, it said on Thursday.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net export sales of US wheat in the week ended November 12 at 344,800 metric tons in the current marketing year, within a range of trade expectations for 200,000 to 400,000 tons.

  • CBOT December soft red winter wheat settled 8-1/4 cents higher at $5.78-1/4 per bushel after dipping to $5.65-1/4, the contract's lowest since January.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) last traded up 17-3/4 cents at $6.27 a bushel.

  • Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) rose 13 cents to end at $6.41-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: Endava Receives Notice from NYSE Regarding Delayed Filing of Annual Report on Form 20-F
data.description:
Endava plc () (“Endava” or the “Company”) today announced that it received a notice from the New York Stock Exchange (the “NYSE”) on November 18, 2026 stating that the Company is not in compliance with the NYSE’s continued listing requirements under Section 802.01E of the NYSE Listed Company Manual as a result of the Company’s delay in filing its Annual Report on Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 (the “Annual Report”) with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”).

The notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company’s securities on the NYSE subject to the Company’s compliance with other continued listing requirements.

As previously disclosed in a Form 12b-25 filed by the Company on November 3, 2026, the Company was unable, without unreasonable effort or expense, to file the Annual Report within the prescribed time period due to the internal investigation initiated by the Company’s Audit Committee into the accounting treatment of certain customer and supplier agreements. As a result of the investigation and the identification of separate accounting errors relating to revenue recognition, the Company is in the process of restating its previously reported financial results for fiscal 2026.

The Company’s preliminary estimate of the restatement’s impact on the Company’s previously reported fiscal 2026 financial results, its disclosure controls and procedures, and its internal control over financial reporting remains consistent with its press release issued on October 28, 2026. Endava expects adjustments to its fiscal 2026 revenue to be equivalent to approximately 2% – 4% of the Company’s fiscal 2025 revenue, it does not expect any adjustments to its fiscal 2025 results, and it does not expect a restatement of prior fiscal years or previous periods relating to those prior fiscal years. Management is currently in discussions with its lenders as it evaluates these matters and the potential impact on the Company’s revolving credit facility.

Under NYSE rules, Endava has a six-month period from the filing due date of November 17, 2026 to file the Annual Report with the SEC and regain compliance. The Company continues to work diligently with its advisors and auditors to file the Annual Report as soon as reasonably practicable and regain compliance with the NYSE’s continued listing requirements.

About Endava

Endava is a leading provider of next-generation technology services dedicated to enabling its clients to accelerate growth, tackle complex challenges and thrive in evolving markets. Endava embeds AI across the design and delivery of technology transformation, combining it with deep industry expertise to deliver measurable client outcomes with greater speed and precision. Central to Endava’s model is Dava.Flow™, its AI-native engagement lifecycle with governance, traceability and transparency built into the delivery process.

Endava’s clients span payments, insurance, banking and capital markets, technology, media, telecommunications, healthcare, mobility, retail and consumer goods and more. The Company’s team of more than 10,000 Endavans helps clients break new ground from locations in Europe, the Americas, Asia Pacific and the Middle East.

For more information, visit www.endava.com.

data.title: Diversified Energy Completes Birch Acquisition
data.description:
Diversified Energy Company (; ) ("Diversified" or the "Company") announces the close, on November 19, 2026, of its previously announced, accretive acquisition of Birch Permian Holdings, Inc. and certain affiliated companies (collectively, "Birch") from its former owners (the "Sellers") (the "Acquisition"). The Acquisition adds complementary operated producing properties and acreage positions in the Permian Basin (the "Assets"). In conjunction with the closing of the Acquisition, the Company closed on a $1,455 million asset backed securitization ("ABS XIV"), TCG Capital Markets L.L.C. served as Sole Structuring Agent and Sole Placement Agent on the financing. CIBC Capital Markets provided an LC Liquidity Facility to meet the liquidity reserve requirements.

Rusty Hutson, Jr., Chairman and CEO of Diversified, commented:

"We are excited to announce the closing of Birch, which delivers high-quality producing assets, durable cash flow, and a contiguous Permian Basin position. This highly accretive acquisition is exactly the type of transaction we focus on, where we can optimize the assets using our vertical integration and scale to meaningfully increase free cash flow for shareholders."

Acquisition Highlights

  • Net production of 68 Mboepd (409 MMcfepd)(a)
    -- 35% production increase to standalone Diversified(a)

    -- 70% liquids and 30% natural gas(a)
  • Gross purchase price of $1,800 million with a purchase price multiple of 3.3x on NTM Adjusted EBITDA(b)
    -- Gross purchase price adjusted by customary amounts including
    interim cash flows and working capital liabilities; minimal DEC liquidity required at closing
    -- Estimated NTM Adjusted EBITDA of $548 million(b), before
    anticipated synergies
  • PDP reserves of 1,168 Bcfe(c) and PV-10 of $2.0 billion(d)

ABS Issuance Highlights

  • $1,455 million ABS notes structured as a master trust; Acquisition closing directly into the ABS eliminated the need for an acquisition bridge facility, reducing financing costs
  • Anchored by funds managed by The Carlyle Group "Carlyle", through the Company's strategic partnership with Carlyle, which was expanded to up to $10 billion of growth capital at the announcement of the Acquisition
  • The A tranche notes priced at a blended coupon of 6.84%, benefited by an investment-grade rating

2026 Impact

  • Birch is expected to add $50 million of Adjusted EBITDA to Q4 2026 results

Forward-Looking Statements

These forward-looking statements, which contain the words "anticipate", "believe", "intend", "estimate", "expect", "may", "will", "seek", "continue", "aim", "target", "projected", "plan", "goal", "achieve", "opportunity" and words of similar meaning, reflect the Company's beliefs and expectations and are based on numerous assumptions regarding the Company's present and future business strategies and the environment the Company will operate in and are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially. Many of these risks and uncertainties relate to factors that are beyond the Company's ability to control or estimate precisely, including the risk factors described in the "Risk Factors" section in the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and in the Company's Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, each filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission. Forward-looking statements speak only as of their date and neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, employees, agents, affiliates or advisers undertakes any obligation to supplement, amend, update or revise any of the forward-looking statements made herein, except where it would be required to do so under applicable law. As a result, you are cautioned not to place undue reliance on such forward-looking statements.

Adjusted EBITDA

As used herein, EBITDA represents earnings before interest, taxes, depletion, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA includes adjustments for items that are not comparable period-over-period, namely, finance costs, accretion of asset retirement obligation, other (income) expense, (gain) loss on fair value adjustments of unsettled financial instruments, (gain) loss on natural gas and oil property and equipment, (gain) loss on sale of equity interest, unrealized (gain) loss on investment, costs associated with acquisitions, other adjusting costs, loss on early retirement of debt, non-cash equity compensation, (gain) loss on interest rate swaps, and items of a similar nature.

Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for operating profit or loss, net income or loss, or cash flows provided by operating, investing and financing activities. However, we believe such measure is useful to an investor in evaluating our financial performance because it (1) is widely used by investors in the natural gas and oil industry as an indicator of underlying business performance; (2) helps investors to more meaningfully evaluate and compare the results of our operations from period to period by removing the often-volatile revenue impact of changes in the fair value of derivative instruments prior to settlement; (3) is used in the calculation of a key metric in one of our Credit Facility financial covenants; and (4) is used by us as a performance measure in determining executive compensation. When evaluating this measure, we believe investors also commonly find it useful to evaluate this metric as a percentage of our total revenue, inclusive of settled hedges, producing what we refer to as our Adjusted EBITDA margin. We are unable to provide a quantitative reconciliation of forward-looking Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable forward-looking GAAP measure because the items necessary to estimate such forward-looking GAAP measure are not accessible or estimable at this time without unreasonable efforts. Reconciling items in future periods could be significant.

PV-10

PV-10 is a non-GAAP financial measure that differs from a financial measure under GAAP known as "standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows" in that PV-10 is calculated without including future income taxes and discounted at 10 percent. The Company believes the presentation of PV-10 provides useful information because it is widely used by investors in evaluating oil and natural gas companies without regard to specific income tax characteristics of such entities. PV-10 is not intended to represent the current market value of the Company's estimated proved reserves. PV-10 should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the standardized measure as defined under GAAP.

data.description:
DWS Municipal Income Trust (NYSE:KTF) (the “Fund”) announced today the payment of its final liquidating distribution to shareholders of $8.290 per share. Liquidation proceeds are expected to be disbursed on Monday, November 23, 2026. The liquidating distribution is being made pursuant to the Fund’s Plan of Liquidation and Termination, as announced on July 17, 2026. The liquidating distribution represents all of the Fund’s remaining net assets except for amounts set aside for reasonably ascertainable liabilities and obligations of the Fund.

Deutsche Asset Management expresses its appreciation to the shareholders who have supported the Fund and its Board over the years.

Important Information

Bond investments are subject to interest-rate, credit, liquidity and market risks to varying degrees. When interest rates rise, bond prices generally fall. Credit risk refers to the ability of an issuer to make timely payments of principal and interest. Municipal securities are subject to the risk that litigation, legislation or other political events, local business or economic conditions or the bankruptcy of the issuer could have a significant effect on an issuer’s ability to make payments of principal and/or interest. The market for municipal bonds may be less liquid than for taxable bonds and there may be less information available on the financial condition of issuers of municipal securities than for public corporations. Investing in derivatives entails special risks relating to liquidity, leverage and credit that may reduce returns and/or increase volatility. Leverage results in additional risks and can magnify the effect of any gains or losses. Although the fund seeks income that is exempt from federal income taxes, a portion of the fund’s distributions may be subject to federal, state and local taxes, including the alternative minimum tax.

Closed-end funds, unlike open-end funds, are not continuously offered. There is a one-time public offering and once issued, shares of closed-end funds are bought and sold in the open market through a stock exchange. Shares of closed-end funds frequently trade at a discount to the net asset value. The price of a fund’s shares is determined by a number of factors, several of which are beyond the control of the fund. Therefore, the fund cannot predict whether its shares will trade at, below or above net asset value.

Past performance is no guarantee of future results.

data.title: Bausch + Lomb Reports Phase 2 Findings for BL1332 in Post-Surgical Ocular Pain
data.description:
Bausch + Lomb Corporation (NYSE/), a leading global eye health company dedicated to helping people see better to live better, today announced topline results from a Phase 2 study evaluating BL1332, a first-in-class topical TRPV1 antagonist, in patients experiencing pain following photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) surgery.

“What stands out from this study is the consistency of the findings,” said Yehia Hashad, MD, executive vice president, R&D and chief medical officer, Bausch + Lomb. “Both dose groups showed numerically greater pain relief than vehicle across all the pain measures we evaluated, more patients achieved complete pain relief following surgery and we observed evidence of faster corneal healing. These findings help define the clinical profile of BL1332 and will inform our discussions with the FDA on next steps, including potential Phase 3 planning.”

Ocular surface pain is a common and often debilitating condition that can occur following surgery and in association with a variety of ocular disorders. Despite its prevalence, there are currently no approved therapies specifically designed to target the underlying neurosensory pathways responsible for ocular surface pain.

BL1332 is a first-in-class topical TRPV1 antagonist designed to block a key receptor involved in ocular pain signaling. Unlike therapies that primarily address associated signs or symptoms, BL1332 is intended to directly modulate the biological pathways that drive ocular pain.

Study Design and Results

The randomized, double-masked, vehicle-controlled, parallel-group Phase 2 study evaluated BL1332 0.30% and BL1332 0.15% ophthalmic solution versus vehicle in 129 adults undergoing unilateral sequential PRK surgery for myopia. Participants were randomized 2:2:1 to BL1332 0.30%, BL1332 0.15% or vehicle and received treatment beginning immediately after surgery, with five doses administered over 24 hours while awake for three days and follow-up through Day 14.

The study was designed to identify an initial efficacy signal and characterize the clinical profile of BL1332 in post-surgical patients.

The study did not meet its primary endpoint of demonstrating a statistically significant improvement versus vehicle in the sum of pain intensity differences (SPID) over 24 hours. The least-squares mean difference versus vehicle was -11.5 for BL1332 0.30% and -9.0 for BL1332 0.15%, with negative values favoring BL1332 indicating greater pain relief.

Both BL1332 dose groups demonstrated numerically greater pain relief than vehicle across every SPID analysis conducted, including the primary endpoint, secondary endpoints and exploratory analyses through 72 hours after surgery. Consistent directional improvement was observed across all prespecified pain assessment windows.

For the secondary endpoint measuring pain reduction during the first six hours after surgery, the 0.30% dose demonstrated a nominally significant reduction versus vehicle.

Exploratory Findings

Additional exploratory analyses provided further insight into the clinical profile of BL1332.

At every assessment between six and 12 hours after surgery, a greater proportion of patients receiving either BL1332 dose reported complete pain relief compared with vehicle. At six hours following surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14.0% and 14.6% of patients receiving BL1332 0.30% and 0.15%, respectively, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving vehicle.

In an anterior segment OCT subset, patients treated with either BL1332 dose demonstrated greater central corneal epithelial thickness at Day 3 compared with vehicle. These findings were consistent with faster healing of the corneal surface following surgery and support further evaluation in future studies.

Safety

BL1332 was well tolerated.

Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 6.0% of patients receiving BL1332 0.30%, 13.7% of patients receiving BL1332 0.15% and 14.8% of patients receiving vehicle. There were no treatment-related adverse events, serious adverse events or discontinuations due to adverse events.

The safety profile was considered acceptable, with no new safety signals identified.

Path Forward

Bausch + Lomb is completing its analysis of the full dataset and expects to discuss the findings with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

The company is evaluating study designs, endpoints and patient populations that best align with the clinical profile observed in this study. These findings, together with results from a previously reported Phase 1b study of BL1332 in participants with capsaicin-induced pain, will help shape discussions with the FDA and the program's future development.

Call with R&D Leadership

Today at 5 p.m. ET, Dr. Hashad and Mayssa Attar, PhD, senior vice president, Pharmaceuticals and Consumer R&D, Bausch + Lomb, will present the results followed by a Q&A session. Details:

data.title: Assurant Board of Directors Approves Common Stock Dividend Increase of 9%
data.description:
Assurant, Inc. (), a global company that redefines the boundaries of protection – safeguarding and servicing connected devices, homes, automobiles, and commercial equipment in partnership with the world’s leading brands, today announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly dividend increase of $0.08 to $0.96 per share of common stock. The dividend will be payable on December 28, 2026 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on December 7, 2026.

“Twenty-two consecutive years of dividend growth reflects the strength and resilience of our businesses. Since our 2004 initial public offering, Assurant’s quarterly dividend has grown more than 13x, or a compound annual growth rate of more than 12%,” said Assurant Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Keith Meier. “Strong cash flow, market-leading positions in Global Lifestyle and Global Housing, and focused execution, backed by a strong balance sheet, allow us to invest in long-term growth while returning capital to shareholders,” Meier added.

Future dividend declarations will be made at the discretion of the Assurant Board of Directors and will depend on various factors, including the company’s earnings, financial condition, capital requirements, subsidiaries’ payments of dividends to the company, future prospects, regulatory restrictions and other considerations.

About Assurant

Assurant, Inc. () redefines the boundaries of protection – safeguarding and servicing connected devices, homes, automobiles, and commercial equipment in partnership with the world’s leading brands. As a Fortune 500 company operating in 21 countries, Assurant leads the way in leveraging insights and technology to transform customer connections that build loyalty and drive value.

Learn more at assurant.com.
